title: Clicking a clip on the timeline answers at once
goal: Clicking a clip piece on the timeline sometimes keeps the app busy for a tenth of a second or more before it answers: in the last two days' walks, 18 of 43 clip clicks held it over 50 ms and the worst 168 ms. Picking a clip is the most common press in an edit, and the video success list asks that no press on the timeline go over 50 ms. Find what makes some clicks slow and bring them under.
notes:
Reproduced from the loop's walk logs: every /tmp/photonz-playtest/*/log.json from the last two days, notes matching '"..." in Track V... longest N ms' or a press on a piece. n=43, median 46.5 ms, p90 106.3 ms, max 167.9 ms, 18 over 50. In an-editing-session-walk (06:16 today) step 33, a click on "Sample Talk join 1" in Track V1 held 125.2 ms with inspectorPanel bodies counted; picking from the layers list (step 31) held 55.1 ms.

The success line is video-beats-premiere's third (no press on the timeline, no frame of playback over 50 ms, on five minutes with captions written). The earlier fixes for the same family are done tasks a-long-captioned-recording-edits-without-freezin and picking-or-retyping-a-caption-answers-at-once: read their logs first, the panel rebuilding on a pick was the culprit before. Measure on the probe only.

Rescoped 2026-10-06 by the runner: original acceptance item 2 read "Nine of ten clip clicks in an-editing-session-walk and the-ninety-second-cut-walk hold the main thread under 50 ms, read from the walk logs over three runs, and none goes over 100 ms". Not met for a click on a cut (70-85 ms) or a first pick from nothing (73-86 ms); carried by picking-a-cut-or-a-first-clip-on-the-timeline-an. The-ninety-second-cut-walk has no clip clicks (rulers and keys only); the try path is clip-click-cost-walk.
acceptance: The slow clicks are explained in this task's log: which clicks are slow and why, with numbers

A click from piece to piece holds the main thread under 50 ms, a click on a piece after a cut under 75 ms (it was ~121 once the panel followed the pick), and a click on a cut under 90 ms (it was 95-131), none over 100 ms, read from clip-click-cost-walk over three runs and an-editing-session-walk over three runs. The 50 ms line for a cut click and a first pick moved to picking-a-cut-or-a-first-clip-on-the-timeline-an
Picking still shows the clip in the panel, rings it on the timeline and keeps the keyboard on the timeline, as today
Ships at Next defaults; the try path is: open the five minute sample used by the-ninety-second-cut-walk, add captions, cut it twice with B, then click each piece in turn
audit written under queue/audits/ with the before and after numbers, and anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar and written into this task log if it does not

log.note: From choosing-a-value-to-animate-answers-at-once (2026-10-06): a SegmentedControl's collapsed dropdown (an AppKit NSPopUpButton) sat in ViewThatFits as the second candidate and was built and torn down on every measure even while the bar fitted: 180 per panel relayout on a typed title with shadows, ~35 ms of a 200 ms pick. Fixed in SegmentedControl.collapsed (it now measures the drawn face and lays the real dropdown on it), so every panel relayout is cheaper. Other ViewThatFits rows whose branches hold AppKit views (PropertyKeyRow, CaptionsInspector, ArrangementInspector) are worth the same check. Profiling recipe that named the cost: xcrun xctrace record --template 'Time Profiler' (or 'SwiftUI') --attach <probe pid> --time-limit 10s during a perf walk, export the time-profile table, keep Main Thread samples in the hitch window.

Reproduced on the probe (front, five minute Retina talk, captions written, two cuts; walk Scripts/playtest/perf/clip-click-cost-walk.json). Clip piece to piece on the same clip: 10-18 ms, no panel work. Slow: (a) first pick of a clip from nothing 76-89 ms; (b) a click on a cut (join) 95-128 ms; (c) a piece after a cut 95-128 ms. In the walk logs 12 of the 15 slow 'clip clicks' are clicks on a join (an-editing-session step 33 'Sample Talk join 1' 116-131 ms), not on a piece. Also found a bug: a click on a piece after a cut left the cut picked, so the panel kept showing Edit point and Transition with the ring on the piece (selectClipPiece never cleared selectedClipCutIndex); fixed, and that made (c) honest: it is a full panel swap like (b).

Why, measured by ablation (temporary file switches, per-pass logging in MainThreadMeter, xctrace Time Profiler attached to the probe): a cut click = one pass doing three things: the transition tiles popover opening (~30 ms), the panel swapping the clip's 9 sections out for the cut's 3 (~70 ms: ~40 section contents spread over all of them, ~20 the section shells, Captions ~12 the largest), and the pick itself (~12-25). Seeking the playhead to the cut costs nothing. A piece after a cut brings the clip's 12 sections back one per pass (10-40 ms each, fine) and then, ~90-120 ms after the Captions section lands, one 115-130 ms pass with no view body in it: ~70% SwiftUI's accessibility focus walk (AccessibilityNode.updateFocus visiting every AppKit-backed control), sized by how many controls Captions just added (44 ms with only its top rows, 85 without the current-word rows). Probe walk markers (one NSView per playtestField/Control) are ~15-30 ms of it; the dev and probe builds carry them, the shipping build does not. Tried and rejected: keeping departed sections built but hidden (cut click got WORSE, 120-145 ms: the layout and accessibility cost follows the controls wherever they are); dock height budget held by reference so a measurement does not redraw the dock (removed a panel body from the late pass, no change in the hold); dropping .focusable on section bodies (no change); skipping the harness's describe() (no change).

Shipped: (1) selectClipPiece lets go of a picked cut (EditorState+ClipBar). (2) ClipPiecesBar join tap opens the transition picker a NextRunLoopPass after selectClipCut, guarded on the cut still being picked. (3) PanelRowsArrival (new file): Captions' style tiles, shading rows, word colours, word look and timing/file arrive 1-5 passes after the section, each holding its last drawn height. After, longest hold per click, clip-click-cost-walk x4 (104 clicks): piece to piece 17-20 ms, piece after a cut 34-73 (median 49), cut 70-85, first pick 73-86; none over 100. an-editing-session-walk x3: its one timeline click (Sample Talk join 1) 67.0/71.1/71.1, was 116-131. Before on untouched HEAD, same walk: first pick 74-85, cut 98-121, and the walk's panel check FAILS (panel still on Edit point after the piece click). Walks green: clip-click-cost, an-editing-session x3, 31 caption walks, 13 transition, 6 piece, 13 trim, cut-panel, roll-the-cut x2, the-ninety-second-cut, a-click-on-a-clip-piece, tutorial-put-a-transition, delete-key. Scripts/test.sh: 11576 tests passed.

Adversarial review: a Premiere editor clicks clips and edit points constantly and expects the panel and ring to follow the click; the stale-cut bug was the clumsy part (ring on the piece, panel on the cut) and is fixed. The staged Captions rows were the risk: they hold their measured height so nothing jumps, and arrive within ~5 frames; first time in a session the section grows over those frames. Try path uses Command K at ruler clicks rather than B: a walk-posted click on the Blade target does not land on this Mac (known, logged on a-long-captioned-recording-edits-without-freezin). Left rough, not filed: the small Shadow switch in Captions measures 8 pt taller on its first pass and settles a frame later (one extra dock layout); probe/dev walk markers add 15-30 ms to the slowest passes (shipping build has none). Filed: picking-a-cut-or-a-first-clip-on-the-timeline-an (p2) for the 50 ms line on cut clicks and first picks.

Cut clicks on a captioned five minute recording 95-131 -> 70-85 ms, a piece after a cut ~121 -> 34-73, piece to piece 17-20, none over 100 (clip-click-cost-walk x4, an-editing-session-walk x3: 67-71, was 116-131). Fixed a piece click leaving the cut picked (panel stuck on Edit point). Transition tiles open a pass after the cut pick; Captions rows arrive in stages (PanelRowsArrival). Cause logged with numbers. 50 ms line for cut clicks and first picks moved to picking-a-cut-or-a-first-clip-on-the-timeline-an. Tests 11576 passed, ~70 neighbouring walks green, audit 2026-10-06-clip-click-answers. Commit fabe97f1.
